sentences.text: This judgmentcumaward shall decide the claim petition of Mukesh Kumar filed  under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter  referred to as "M.V. Act") as amended up to date to claim compensation for the  injuries sustained by him in an accident caused by a Crane that took place on  25.08.2017.

FIR No.570/17 u/ss 287/338 IPC was registered at Police Station  Ranhola and chargesheet was filed against respondent No.1/Arun Kumar,
 driver of Hydra Ace Crane bearing registration No.HR51BP9160 (offending  vehicle).
 2.
Copies of criminal proceedings including FIR, chargesheet, site plan etc. were  filed by the petitioner.

3. Brief facts of the vehicular accident as averred in the claim petition are that at  about 10:00 AM on 25.08.2017, petitioner Mukesh Kumar along with other  workers was helping respondent No.1/driver of the offending Crane in lifting  and shifting a cutter machine into factory.
The driver of the offending Crane was  driving the crane in a rash and negligent manner without taking safety  precautions.
Due to his negligent act, cutter machine fell down from the grip of  the crane and fell over the right leg of the petitioner.
Resultantly, petitioner  sustained grievous injuries.
He was removed to Rathi Hospital and then to AIIMS  Trauma Centre for better treatment.
4. Subsequently, it transpired that the offending Crane was owned by respondent  No.2/Makhan Lal Shah and insured with respondent No.3/
HDFC ERGO General  Insurance Company Ltd.

5. In the joint Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e.
 driver and owner, it was averred that the accident took place solely due to  negligence of petitioner as he was not vigilant while performing his duties at the  site.
It was also claimed that since the offending vehicle was duly insured with  respondent No.3/insurance company, hence, no liability can be fastened upon  them.

3 6. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.3/insurance company,
 it was claimed that the FIR was registered u/s 287/338 IPC and not u/s 279 IPC  as respondent No.1/driver did not commit any offence due to rash and negligent  driving.
It was also averred that petitioner himself was responsible for sustaining  injuries due to his own negligence.

It was, however, admitted that the alleged  offending vehicle was insured with it vide its Policy bear  No.2316201832990500000 valid from 30.06.2017 to 29.06.2018.
7.
In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.4/Santosh Gupta  alleged to have hired the offending vehicle from respondent No.2/Makhan Lal  Shah/Registered Owner
, it was averred that at the time of accident, respondent  No.4 was neither the registered owner nor the hirer of the alleged offending  vehicle.
It is was, thus, stated that no liability can be fastened upon him.

10. My findings on the issues are as under:
 ISSUE NO.1:
 Whether the petitioner Mukesh Kumar suffered grievous injuries in a  vehicular accident that took place on 25.08.2017 at about 10:00 AM  at H.No.937, Gali No.15, Kotla Vihar, PhaseII, Ranhola, Najafgarh,
 Delhi involving a Hydra Ace Crane bearing registration No.HR51BP  9680, driven by respondent No.1/Arun Kumar, owned by respondent  No.2/Makhan Lal and insured with respondent No.3/HDFC ERGO  General Insurance Company Ltd.?

sentences.text: OPP  4 11.

In a claim petition filed under u/s 166/140 of the M.V. Act, onus is on the  claimant(s)/petitioner(s) to prove that he or she sustained injuries in a vehicular  accident caused by the wrongful act or negligence of the driver of the offending  vehicle.
12.

In support of his claim, petitioner Mukesh Kumar examined himself as PW1;
 Ms.Shilpi Kushwaha, Prosthetist & Orthotist, P&O International Pvt.Ltd. as PW2  and Dr.Naresh Chandra, Specialist & HOD(Ortho), Guru Govind Singh  Govt.Hospital as PW3.

13. In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex.PW1/A), petitioner Mukesh Kumar (PW1)
 explained the mode and manner of the accident as described in para 3 of this  award.

14. In his crossexamination by respondents, it was denied by petitioner Mukesh  Kumar that he had sustained injuries due to his own negligence, inspite of the  warning given by his employer Santosh Gupta.
Rather, the incident was  explained in detail by the petitioner PW1.
It was testified by him that a heavy  cutter machine was to be lifted with the help of the offending vehicle from  outside the factory premises to inside the factory premises.
In order to lift the  machine, the clamping was done by the driver of the crane with the help of iron  chains.
He further testified that his employer/Santosh Gupta had directed him  and 45 other employees to lift the machine with iron chains.
When the machine  was lifted at a height of about 8 feet, the cutter machine fell from the crane on  the petitioner, inside the factory.
15. The scrutiny of the testimony of PW1/Mukesh Kumar, petitioner, reflects that  the cutter machine fell on him as the machine was not secured with the clamp  properly by the driver of the crane.

In his testimony, R1W1/Arun Kumar, driver  of the crane admitted that at the time of the accident, it was he, who was Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/
3  operating the offending crane.
He also admitted that the machine was secured  with iron chain by him with the help of 34 labourers.

16. In view of the testimony of PW1/Mukesh Kumar and R1W1/Arun Kumar, it can  be safely concluded that the accident took place due rash and negligent act of  R1W1/Anil Kumar while the offending crane was put in motion by R1W1/Anil  Kumar.
Considering the facts and circumstances, it is accordingly held that the accident  took place due to negligent act of respondent No.1/Arun Kumar.
Issue No.1

is,
 thus, decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

18. Finding on Issue No.2:
 Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what  amount and from whom? OPP 19.
In RAJ KUMAR VS. AJAY KUMAR & ANOTHER (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble  Supreme Court of India has laid down general principles for computation of  compensation in injury cases.

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced  as under:
 5.

The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes   clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to  the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position  prior to the accident.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss  suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair,
 reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to  assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation  or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability an  its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for th  physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such  injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a fu  life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoye  but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or  could have earned.
 6.

The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases  are the following:
 Pecuniary damages (special damages)
 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
 nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made  had he not been injured, comprising:
 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability  (iii) Future medical expenses.

Nonpecuniary damages (general damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under  heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where the  specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that  compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and  (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability,
 future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/
4  marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

6 PECUNIARY DAMAGES (Special Damages)
 Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines 20.
Petitioner Mukesh Kumar/PW1 in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex.PW1/A)
deposed that immediately after the accident, he was removed to Rathi Hospital  and thereafter, he was shifted to AIIMS Trauma Centre.

PW1 placed on record  Discharge Summary (Ex.PW1/14, colly), as per which, he was admitted to JPN  Trauma Centre on 25.08.2017 and discharged on 02.09.2017 with diagnosis of  "Crush injury right lower limb".
It was also testified by him that during his  treatment, his right leg above knee was amputated.
The said fact was neither  disputed nor controverted by the respondents.
It was further claimed by the  petitioner that he had spent Rs.50,000/ on his treatment.
However, petitioner  placed on record medical bills (Ex.PW1/14, colly) amounting to Rs.1,065/ only.
Admittedly, the petitioner was treated at government hospital

, petitioner is,
 thus, held entitled to a compensation of Rs.1,065/ (Rupees One Thousand  and Sixty Five) under this head.
Expenses relating to Conveyance, Food(Special Diet) and Attendant charges 21.

Taking into account the amputation of right leg above knee, an amount of  Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty Thousand) towards Conveyance and Rs.35,000/
 (Rupees Thirty Five Thousand) towards Special Diet is awarded as  compensation.
22. Petitioner is further awarded a compensation of Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty  Thousand) towards attendant charges.
Loss of earning during the period of treatment 23.
To prove that the injuries sustained by the petitioner resulted in amputation of  his right leg above knee and that he suffered disability, petitioner examined  PW3/Dr.Naresh Chandra.
PW3/Dr.Naresh Chandra testified that he had  examined the petitioner Mukesh Kumar for assessment of his physical disability.

PW3 further testified that Medical Board had assessed his permanent physical  disability vide Disability Certificate (Ex.PW3/A), as per which, petitioner was  found to be suffering from physical disability to the extent of 80% in relation to  his right lower limb.
24. Although, it was claimed by petitioner that he was a labour in M/s System  7  Aircon and earning Rs.16,500/ at the time of accident, but no document  regarding his income was placed on record.
Petitioner, however, placed on  record his 12th class markssheet (Ex.PW1/15, colly).
Hence, petitioner is  considered as a Matriculate as per Minimum Wages Rate prevailing in Delhi.

Accordingly, income of the petitioner Mukesh Kumar is assessed as Rs.16,182/
 per month as on the date of accident.
25. Considering the vocation of the petitioner that he was a labour, his functional  disability is considered as 100% in relation to his whole body.
Compensation on account of loss of earning capacity 26.

In a judgment titled as JAGDISH VS. MOHAN AND OTHERS, reported as 2018 ACJ  1011 delivered by three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Hon'ble  Supreme Court awarded compensation towards loss of future prospects in a case  where the petitioner had sustained physical disability of 90% due to amputation  of both his hands.

In view of the ratios in the aforecited cases, it is imperative to calculate  compensation towards loss of future prospects to ascertain compensation on  account of loss of earning in the instant case.
28. To prove his age, petitioner placed on record his Aadhar Card (Ex.PW1/16), as  per which, his date of birth was 08.01.1998.
Since the accident took place on  25.08.2017
, hence, he was aged 19 years at the time of accident.

In view of the  ratio of judgment titled as NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY VS. PRANAY SETHI  & ORS. decided on 31.10.2017 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, an addition of  40% of Rs.16,182/ (Rs.6,472.80 p.m.) is made towards future prospects in the  income of the petitioner/injured. Thus, total monthly income of the petitioner  after making an addition of future prospects would be Rs.22,654.80 per month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 29. Accordingly, loss of future earning on account of physical disability of petitioner  amounts to Rs.22,654.80 per month (Rs.22,654.80 x 100%).
Hence, annual  8  loss of future earning of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.2,71,857.60  (Rs.22,654.80 x 12) which is ascertained as multiplicand.
Multiplier 30.

Since petitioner was aged 19 years at the time of the accident, hence, applying  the criteria of multiplier laid down in SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS. DELHI  TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER, (2009) 6 SUPREME COURT CASES  121, the multiplier applicable in this case would be 18 (eighteen).
31.

 Future Medical Expenses 32.

It was claimed by the petitioner PW1/Mukesh Kumar that he would require a  prosthetic limb to enable him in his day to day activities, which would cost him  about Rs.3,44,985/ as per quotation dated 13.09.2018.

In support of his claim,
 petitioner examined PW2/Ms.Shilpi Kushwaha, Prosthetist and Orthotist, who  testified that Quotation (Ex.PW1/13) amounting to Rs.3,08,022/ plus GST was  issued by P&O International Pvt.Ltd. in favour of injured/petitioner Mukesh  Kumar.
33.
Admittedly, petitioner has not procured any prosthetic limb till date.

It is,
 accordingly, held that in case, petitioner acquires any prosthetic limb, the cost  of the same shall be borne by the insurance company/respondent No.3,
 subject to production of original bills. It is also made clear that in case,
 petitioner needs replacement of any component of his Prosthetic limb, the  expenses for its replacement, if any, will also be borne by the insurance  company/respondent No.3 subject to production of original medical bills.

NONPECUNIARY DAMAGES (GENERAL DAMAGES)
 Pain, Suffering & Trauma 34.

In R.D. HATTANGADI VS. PEST CONTROL (INDIA) PVT.LTD., I (1995) ACC 281  (SC), where a road accident resulted in 100% disability due to paraplegia below  waist to a lawyer (retired Judge), the Supreme Court observed as under:
 9 Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/
6  "That no amount of compensation can restore the physical frame of the  appellant.

entities.text: R.D. HATTANGADI VS. PEST CONTROL (INDIA) PVT.LTD., I (1995) ACC 281  (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is why it has been said by Courts that whenever any  amount is determined as the compensation payable for any injury suffered  during an accident, the object is to compensate such injured "so far as  money can compensate" because it is impossible to equate the money with  the human sufferings or personal deprivations.
Money cannot renew a  broken and shattered physical frame.

In its very nature whenever a Tribunal, or a Court is required to fix the amount of compensation in cases of accident, it involves some guess work, some hypothetical consideration, some amount of sympathy linked with the nature of the disability caused.
But all the aforesaid elements have to be viewed with objective standards.

........................................................ ......................................................... ................................When compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering and loss of amenity of life, the special circumstances of the claimant have to be taken into account including his age, the unusual deprivation he has suffered, the effect thereof on his future life."
35.

Considering the fact that the petitioner lost his right leg above knee due to the accident in question which caused him immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ (Rupees Two Lakhs) would be just and fair compensation under this head.
Loss of amenities of life and disfigurement 36.
Undoubtedly, petitioner has many more years to live ahead and without the aide of one limb, he is sure to suffer in his day to day activities and face hardships.
Hence, petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ (Rupees Two Lakhs) as compensation under this head.

 6. Pain, Suffering & Trauma 2,00  7. Loss of amenities of life and Disfigurement 2,00
Total 54,29,

Accordingly, total compensation is assessed as Rs.54,29,565/ (rounded off to Rs.54,30,000/
)(Rupees Fifty Four Lakhs Thirty Thousand).
LIABILITY 38.

It was very vehemently argued by learned counsel for insurance company that since Section 279 IPC was not invoked, it is evident that the accident had not taken place on a public way and therefore, no liability could be fastened upon insurance company.

The argument of learned counsel for insurance company is without any merit.

In a judgment titled as UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO.LTD. VS. JAGAT & ORS. decided on 28.07.2017 in MAC.APP.55/2012 relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioner, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had upheld the view of Learned Presiding Officer, MACT.

Ors. {2006 (I) T.A.C. 756 (Cal)} and Ram Chandra & Anr. Vs. Shiva Narain & Ors. reported as IV (2006) ACC 838, wherein it was held that if a place is accessible to public, it is a public place even if it is a private property.

sentences.text: In United India Insurance Co.Ltd. (supra), the accident had taken place in the compound of M/s Roadwings International Pvt.Ltd. which was a yard located in Tughlakabad.

It was held that the accident spot cannot be considered as a private place for the reason that public was also allowed entry therein and that wherever public can enter with permission, the said place becomes a public place for the purpose of Motor Vehicle Act.
40. Drawing the analogy from the aforecited case, it is held that the accident spot was a public place.
Accordingly, it is held that insurance company cannot wriggle out of its liability.

41. Since it is proved that respondent No.1/Arun Kumar was the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident, hence, he is liable to pay compensation as the accident took place due to her negligent driving.
Respondent No.2/Makhan Lal Singh is vicariously liable for the conduct of the driver, being the registered owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, since the offending vehicle was duly insured to cover the third party risk, respondent No.3/Insurance company is under statutory liability to pay compensation to the petitioner.
RELIEF 42.
In view of above findings on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I award an amount of Rs.54,30,000/ (Rupees Fifty Four Lakhs Thirty Thousand) as compensation to the petitioner.
Petitioner is also entitled to interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of the Claim Petition i.e. 13.02.2018 till its realisation.
Amount of Interim Award, if paid any, be deducted from the compensation amount.
43. Consequently, interest amount be paid to the petitioner along with award amount as per the terms and conditions mentioned in succeeding paragraphs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The driver of the offending Crane was  driving the crane in a rash and negligent manner without taking safety  precautions.
Due to his negligent act, cutter machine fell down from the grip of  the crane and fell over the right leg of the petitioner.
Resultantly, petitioner  sustained grievous injuries.
He was removed to Rathi Hospital and then to AIIMS  Trauma Centre for better treatment.
It was also claimed that since the offending vehicle was duly insured with  respondent No.3/insurance company, hence, no liability can be fastened upon  them.
In a claim petition filed under u/s 166/140 of the M.V. Act, onus is on the  claimant(s)/petitioner(s) to prove that he or she sustained injuries in a vehicular  accident caused by the wrongful act or negligence of the driver of the offending  vehicle.

Considering the facts and circumstances, it is accordingly held that the accident  took place due to negligent act of respondent No.1/Arun Kumar.

In RAJ KUMAR VS. AJAY KUMAR & ANOTHER (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble  Supreme Court of India has laid down general principles for computation of  compensation in injury cases.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss  suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair,
 reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to  assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation  or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability an  its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for th  physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such  injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a fu  life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoye  but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or  could have earned.
